card.name: Sambai
card.era: Rooted in 18th-c. Afro-Belizean Maroon/Creole culture (Gales Point Manatee); UNESCO-inscribed Dec 2025
card.tagline: Afro-Creole full-moon fertility and courtship dance around a bonfire.
card.profile: The sambai (also 'sambay') is a Creole/Kriol fertility dance from the village of Gales Point Manatee, performed during the full moon and at weddings or birthdays. Per Wikipedia (citing O'Donnell, Adventure Guide to Belize, 2002), it is a solitary dance originally performed by men but now by either gender: the dancer enters a ring of drummers to dance, and when finished points to another person who dances next. The National Kriol Council describes a circle gathered around a pinewood fire; music is led by the goombay (gumbeh) drum with call-and-response chants.
card.insight: The National Kriol Council notes the sambai's link to the full-moon cycle parallels lunar crop cycles, reinforcing its identity as a fertility ritual. It was inscribed by UNESCO in December 2025 (20.COM) as part of 'Christmas Bram and Sambai' (ICH no. 02298) - Belize's second inscription after the 2008 Garifuna listing (UNESCO; National Kriol Council).
